item.title: Former Pensacola Officer Faces Additional Bathroom Photography Allegations
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A former Pensacola Police Department officer arrested on drug and child exploitation charges has additional allegations of taking photographs of adult men in bathroom stalls, according to arresting documents reviewed by Miramar News. The officer was previously arrested on charges involving possession of child sexual abuse material and bestiality…
item.content:encoded:
A former Pensacola Police Department officer arrested on drug and child exploitation charges has additional allegations of taking photographs of adult men in bathroom stalls, according to arresting documents reviewed by Miramar News.

The officer was previously arrested on charges involving possession of child sexual abuse material and bestiality videos. The newly revealed allegations add bathroom voyeurism to the roster of criminal accusations.

Details surrounding the investigation and timeline of the alleged bathroom photography remain limited, but the case underscores the severity of allegations facing the former officer across multiple criminal categories.

item.title: Florida Corrections, Local Law Enforcement Checking Sex Offender Compliance This Halloween
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Florida Department of Corrections is conducting its annual Halloween compliance checks on sex offenders under felony supervision throughout the state, including here in the Panhandle, as part of broader community safety efforts during the holiday season. The statewide initiative involves FDC officials and local law enforcement verifying that…
item.content:encoded:
The Florida Department of Corrections is conducting its annual Halloween compliance checks on sex offenders under felony supervision throughout the state, including here in the Panhandle, as part of broader community safety efforts during the holiday season.

The statewide initiative involves FDC officials and local law enforcement verifying that supervised sex offenders are following the terms of their release, which typically include restrictions on their movements and activities—particularly around times when children are out in public, like trick-or-treating.

Escambia and Santa Rosa County law enforcement agencies participate in these coordinated checks each October 31st. The compliance verifications help ensure offenders registered with the state are where they're supposed to be and adhering to any court-ordered conditions of their supervision.

Florida's sex offender registry and monitoring program is one of the nation's most stringent. Residents can check the Florida Department of Corrections sex offender database online to learn about registered offenders in their neighborhoods.

item.content:encoded: The Pensacola Ice Flyers dominated the Macon Mayhem on Saturday, posting a 5-0 victory in front of a sold-out crowd at the Pensacola Bay Center. item.title: Set Clocks Back Tonight as Daylight Saving Time Ends; Fire Officials Urge Battery Check
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Pensacola-area residents should remember to set their clocks back one hour before bed Saturday night as daylight saving time ends and standard time resumes. Fire officials are also using the time change as a reminder for a critical safety step: replace the batteries in your smoke alarms. The seasonal clock change has become a standard public…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola-area residents should remember to set their clocks back one hour before bed Saturday night as daylight saving time ends and standard time resumes.

Fire officials are also using the time change as a reminder for a critical safety step: replace the batteries in your smoke alarms. The seasonal clock change has become a standard public safety reminder for homeowners to check and refresh smoke detector batteries, which can degrade over time and may not function properly in an emergency.

The twice-yearly time changes — "spring forward" in March and "fall back" in October — have long served as convenient calendar markers for routine home maintenance and safety checks. Residents are encouraged not to let the reminder pass by this year.

item.content:encoded:

Apostolic Life Church is hosting a Fall Festival and Yard Sale today, Saturday, October 31, with the yard sale starting at 8 a.m. The event offers a mix of shopping and seasonal activities for families in the area.

According to North Escambia reporting, additional Halloween and fall festival events are planned throughout the weekend and into next week, giving residents multiple opportunities to get into the holiday spirit. Event details and times for other festivals in the area are available through local community announcements.

item.title: Northview Chiefs Rally Late But Fall Short to Clarke County 38-34

The Chiefs found themselves in an early hole, down 14 points in the first quarter before Judah Woodson scored on a 5-yard fumble return to get Northview on the board at 14-6 with 8:20…
item.content:encoded: The Northview Chiefs mounted a furious second-half comeback Friday night but couldn't quite finish the job, falling 38-34 to Clarke County on Senior Night in Bratt. The Chiefs found themselves in an early hole, down 14 points in the first quarter before Judah Woodson scored on a 5-yard fumble return to get Northview on the board at 14-6 with 8:20 left in the opening quarter. Despite the late surge that brought the game within striking distance, Northview couldn't convert the opportunity into a win, with the decisive moment coming at the goal line. The loss closes out what was billed as a senior celebration for the Chiefs.

Firefighters were dispatched to the 1000 block of Barth Lane at 12:36 p.m. and found smoke billowing from the structure upon arrival. Crews brought the blaze under control by 12:58 p.m. No…
item.content:encoded:
An electrical problem sparked a fire that destroyed a vacant mobile home in the Barth area Thursday afternoon, according to Escambia County Fire Rescue.

Firefighters were dispatched to the 1000 block of Barth Lane at 12:36 p.m. and found smoke billowing from the structure upon arrival. Crews brought the blaze under control by 12:58 p.m.

No injuries were reported. The home was unoccupied at the time of the fire. Escambia County Fire Rescue is continuing to investigate the electrical cause.

item.title: Halloween Trick-or-Treat Weather: Scattered Showers Possible Saturday Evening

item.content:encoded: Halloween revelers in the Pensacola area should keep an eye on the sky Saturday evening, as scattered showers could develop during trick-or-treating hours. The National Weather Service forecast for North Escambia shows a 20 percent chance of showers after 1 p.m., with rain chances increasing overnight into Sunday. Conditions Saturday will be mostly cloudy with a high near 80 degrees and light east winds at 5 to 10 mph. Families heading out for Halloween should have umbrellas handy, particularly as the evening progresses and moisture moves in.

item.title: Last Day To Vote Early In Escambia County Before Tuesday Election
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Today is your final chance to cast an early ballot ahead of Tuesday's general election. Escambia County Supervisor of Elections offices will remain open from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m., and registered voters can visit any early voting location in the county to participate. Early voting has been underway for several weeks leading up to Election Day on…
item.content:encoded:
Today is your final chance to cast an early ballot ahead of Tuesday's general election. Escambia County Supervisor of Elections offices will remain open from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m., and registered voters can visit any early voting location in the county to participate.

Early voting has been underway for several weeks leading up to Election Day on November 3. Voters who don't cast ballots during the early voting period still have the option to vote in person on Election Day at their assigned polling places.

Registered voters can find their polling location and confirm their voter registration status through the Escambia County Supervisor of Elections website.

item.title: Milton residents alarmed over injured alligator with taped mouth, hook in snout

The injured reptile has been a familiar presence in the Santa Rosa County community, and neighbors say they're worried about its welfare and what…
item.content:encoded:
A well-known alligator living near Mulatto Bayou in Milton has become the focus of concern after residents spotted it with its mouth taped shut and a hook lodged in its snout, according to WKRG News 5.

The injured reptile has been a familiar presence in the Santa Rosa County community, and neighbors say they're worried about its welfare and what may have caused the injuries. The discovery has sparked alarm among locals who have grown accustomed to seeing the animal in the area.

It's unclear how the alligator sustained the injuries or whether anyone has reported the incident to wildlife authorities. Residents are hoping the animal receives help to remove the tape and hook before its condition worsens.

item.title: Thomas Hospital opens helipad for emergency air transport

item.content:encoded: Thomas Hospital in Fairhope, Alabama has opened a new emergency helipad, giving medical helicopters direct access to the facility and cutting response times for critically ill or injured patients across the region. According to WKRG News 5, the addition addresses a key gap in trauma care infrastructure—in emergencies, minutes can mean the difference between life and death, and the helipad eliminates delays from ground transport. The new facility is now operational and available for incoming patients requiring rapid air evacuation or transfer to the hospital's emergency department.

Magar, currently Vice President at Heartcare Imaging, Inc., previously served in the Florida House of Representatives from 2012 to 2020, including a stint as Speaker pro tempore from 2018 to 2020. item.content:encoded:
Governor Ron DeSantis announced today the reappointment of MaryLynn Magar to the State Board of Education, pending Florida Senate confirmation.

Magar, currently Vice President at Heartcare Imaging, Inc., previously served in the Florida House of Representatives from 2012 to 2020, including a stint as Speaker pro tempore from 2018 to 2020. She hails from Martin County in South Florida and has been active in local civic organizations, including the Hobe Sound Chamber of Commerce and Northern Palm Beach Chamber of Commerce. She also served as a trustee for All Saints Catholic School.

The appointment requires approval from the state Senate before it becomes final.

item.title: DeSantis Appoints Key West Attorney Andrew Dulcey to Florida Keys Aqueduct Authority

Dulcey currently serves as a board member of the College of the Florida Keys District Board of Trustees and holds membership in the Key West Maritime Historical Society and the Key West International Airport Ad-Hoc…
item.content:encoded:
Governor Ron DeSantis announced Friday the appointment of Andrew Dulcey, a Key West attorney, to the Florida Keys Aqueduct Authority.

Dulcey currently serves as a board member of the College of the Florida Keys District Board of Trustees and holds membership in the Key West Maritime Historical Society and the Key West International Airport Ad-Hoc Committee on Noise. He earned his juris doctor from the University of Miami.

The Florida Keys Aqueduct Authority oversees water supply infrastructure serving the Keys region. The appointment comes as part of the governor's ongoing efforts to fill positions on state boards and authorities across Florida.

item.title: DeSantis Reappoints Four to State Board of Pharmacy, Including Escambia Pharmacist
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Governor Ron DeSantis announced today the reappointment of four members to Florida's Board of Pharmacy, including Darrell Miller, a consultant pharmacist with Escambia County ties. Miller, who previously served as president of the Escambia County Pharmacy Association and held leadership roles at Community Health Northwest Florida and other…
item.content:encoded:
Governor Ron DeSantis announced today the reappointment of four members to Florida's Board of Pharmacy, including Darrell Miller, a consultant pharmacist with Escambia County ties. Miller, who previously served as president of the Escambia County Pharmacy Association and held leadership roles at Community Health Northwest Florida and other regional healthcare organizations, earned his pharmacy degrees from Auburn University and the University of Florida.

The other three reappointees are Leigh Mathes, director of operations for Coastal Med of Florida; Cristina Medina, a pharmacist with CVS Health; and Dorinda Segovia, vice president and chief pharmacy officer for Memorial Healthcare System. All four bring extensive professional credentials and involvement with state and national pharmacy associations.

The appointments require confirmation by the Florida Senate. The Board of Pharmacy oversees licensing, regulation, and discipline of pharmacists and pharmacy operations throughout the state.

item.title: DeSantis Appoints Seven to Florida Board of Medicine; One Has Pensacola Ties
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Governor Ron DeSantis announced appointments and reappointments to the Florida Board of Medicine on Friday, including Dr. Matthew Benson, who earned his undergraduate degree from Pensacola Christian College. Among the appointees is Dr. Andrea Aguilera, a pediatrician with the Emergency Resources Group who previously worked for Nicklaus Children's…
item.content:encoded:
Governor Ron DeSantis announced appointments and reappointments to the Florida Board of Medicine on Friday, including Dr. Matthew Benson, who earned his undergraduate degree from Pensacola Christian College.

Among the appointees is Dr. Andrea Aguilera, a pediatrician with the Emergency Resources Group who previously worked for Nicklaus Children's Health System. Also appointed are Elyse Young, who brings 20 years of state government experience in budgeting and healthcare policy.

Reappointed to the board are Dr. Scot Ackerman, Medical Director of the Ackerman Cancer Center in Jacksonville; Dr. Gobi Balaji, founder and CEO of Brevard Health Center; Dr. Benson, a pediatric endocrinologist at Nemours Children's Health; Dr. Lisa Kay Mao, a clinical ophthalmologist with over 30 years in Florida; and Dr. Hector Vila, an anesthesiologist and owner of Pediatric Dental Anesthesia Associates.

The Board of Medicine regulates physician licensing, discipline, and practice standards across Florida.

item.title: Santa Rosa County November Events: Markets, Music, Racing & More
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Santa Rosa County is packed with entertainment and community activities this November, according to a roundup from Santa Rosa County Communications & Media Relations. For farmers market fans, the Navarre Farmers' Market runs every Saturday from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. at Combs of Honey (Highway 87 & Segura Corner, across from Tractor Supply). You'll find…
item.content:encoded:
Santa Rosa County is packed with entertainment and community activities this November, according to a roundup from Santa Rosa County Communications & Media Relations.

For farmers market fans, the Navarre Farmers' Market runs every Saturday from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. at Combs of Honey (Highway 87 & Segura Corner, across from Tractor Supply). You'll find fresh local produce, dairy, baked goods including gluten-free options, handcrafted soaps and candles, and live plants. The Highway 87 Outdoor Market at Pik-itz also opens Saturdays, 9 a.m.–2 p.m., featuring farm-to-table vendors and arts & crafts.

Music and entertainment venues are active throughout the month. Juana's Pagodas hosts live music Friday and Saturday nights from 8 p.m. to midnight at Navarre Beach (free admission), while Andy D's on Navarre Beach features live music from local and regional acts on varying nights. Stripes Pub & Grill in Navarre has UFC fights, comedy shows, and live music scheduled, and Beardless Brewhaus in downtown Milton hosts Bingo Night every Wednesday at 6:30 p.m.

For outdoor enthusiasts, Holley Hill Pottery in Navarre opens Tuesday through Saturday, 10 a.m.–4 p.m., where visitors can watch potters fire the kiln and browse the gallery. Hunt the Front Southern Speedway in Milton offers dirt track racing most Saturdays, and the Navarre Beach Sea Turtle Rescue Team holds Turtle Chat sessions on Tuesday mornings in November at 10 a.m. at Andy D's.

Looking further ahead, forecasters are also monitoring a potential round of severe weather next week that could impact the area.

item.title: Federal Indictment: Mobile Tax Scheme Sought $177 Million, IRS Paid About $81 Million
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: MOBILE, AL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Federal prosecutors say an alleged tax-fraud operation in Mobile filed more than 9,000 fraudulent returns seeking more than $177 million from the federal government — and approximately $81 million was actually paid out . Six defendants have been indicted in federal court. The U.S. Attorney's Office says Jennifer…
item.content:encoded:
MOBILE, AL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Federal prosecutors say an alleged tax-fraud operation in Mobile filed more than 9,000 fraudulent returns seeking more than $177 million from the federal government — and approximately $81 million was actually paid out.

Six defendants have been indicted in federal court.

The U.S. Attorney's Office says Jennifer Beverly, 47, owned and operated JB Accounting Tax Service in Mobile from approximately 2022 through 2024.

Beverly and five other defendants are accused of participating in a scheme to prepare and submit false federal tax returns between approximately 2021 and 2024.

Prosecutors say the returns contained allegedly fraudulent items including business deductions, COVID-19 credits, fuel-tax credits, estimated tax payments and education credits.

Altogether, the indictment alleges more than 9,000 fraudulent returns sought over $177 million in refunds.

The IRS issued approximately $81 million.

All six defendants are charged with conspiracy to commit wire fraud.

Beverly also faces 63 individual wire-fraud counts, while the other defendants face varying numbers of additional wire-fraud charges.

Federal prosecutors are also seeking forfeiture of alleged proceeds from the scheme. The indictment identifies 12 properties belonging to one or more defendants as potentially subject to forfeiture.

The investigation involves IRS Criminal Investigation and the FBI.

An indictment contains allegations. All six defendants are presumed innocent unless proven guilty in court.
